source.title: 诊断学（第10版）
source.section: 第五篇 辅助检查 第一章 心电图 第六节

textbook_summary: Atrial and ventricular pacemakers operate independently; the atrial rate exceeds the ventricular rate and PR is not fixed.
Junctional escape is generally 40-60/min with normal QRS morphology.
scope: A teaching example of established junctional escape in third-degree AV block.
shape: Reuses existing normal QRS references for twelve-lead and single-lead output without changing electrode projection. Overlapping atrial and ventricular events remain additive.
unimplemented: Broad abnormal QRS morphology for ventricular escape remains unimplemented.
First-escape triggering after arrest and competing pacemakers remain unimplemented.
Retrograde conduction, dynamic loading/contractile feedback and beatwise QT adaptation remain unimplemented.
Atrial flutter, atrial fibrillation, ventricular flutter and ventricular fibrillation remain unimplemented.
constraints: A 1000-1500 ms cycle and a faster atrial rate are example bounds, not diagnostic thresholds. The twelve-lead example exposes only escape period/phase and rejects conflicting morphology/timing controls.
perfusion: CardiacFillingPerfusionIllustration@2: long accepted ventricular RR permits passive filling; independent atrial phase supplies bounded effective assistance. No fixed tachycardia penalty.
